llm-fundamentals.description: Core architectures, Transformer mechanics, self-attention, context windows, tokenization, KV cache, and sampling algorithms.
study_notes: Explain scaled dot-product attention and QKV projection math.
Trade-offs between autoregressive (decoder-only) vs encoder-decoder models.
How KV caching eliminates redundant recomputation during inference.

prompt-engineering.description: Zero/few-shot, Chain-of-Thought (CoT), Tree-of-Thoughts, ReAct, system prompts, structured JSON outputs, and injection defense.
study_notes: Designing resilient system prompts and structured output schema enforcement.
Chain-of-Thought vs Tree-of-Thoughts prompting for complex reasoning.
Mitigating prompt injection and system prompt exfiltration.

rag-and-vector-databases.description: Embeddings, vector indexing (HNSW, IVFFlat), hybrid search, chunking strategies, re-ranking, and query transformation.
study_notes: Dense vs sparse embeddings and hybrid keyword + semantic search.
Chunking strategies (semantic, sliding window) and document parsing.
HNSW vs IVFFlat index tradeoffs for latency, memory, and recall.

ai-agents-and-mcp.description: Agentic workflows, Model Context Protocol (MCP), function calling, tool use, memory persistence, and multi-agent orchestration.
study_notes: Model Context Protocol (MCP) server/client architecture.
ReAct loop mechanics, tool binding, and error recovery.
Managing short-term memory, long-term memory, and state transitions.

fine-tuning-and-adaptation.description: PEFT, LoRA, QLoRA, RLHF, DPO, GRPO, quantization (GGUF, AWQ, GPTQ), model distillation, and domain adaptation.
study_notes: LoRA rank r and alpha scaling factor tuning.
Preference optimization: RLHF vs DPO vs GRPO.
Quantization techniques: INT8/INT4 weight-only vs KV cache quantization.

ai-system-design.description: High-throughput inference, TTFT/TPOT, streaming (SSE), semantic caching, GPU resource planning, and serving infrastructure (vLLM, TGI).
study_notes: Optimizing Time to First Token (TTFT) and Time Per Output Token (TPOT).
PagedAttention, continuous batching, and speculative decoding.
Designing semantic caching layers to reduce API expenses and latency.

llmops-and-production-ai.description: Observability, prompt tracing, cost management, drift detection, CI/CD pipelines for prompts & evals, and production telemetry.
study_notes: Distributed tracing for multi-step agent and RAG pipelines.
Cost budgeting, rate limiting, and fallback LLM routing.
Monitoring model drift, data distribution shift, and latency SLAs.

evaluation-and-testing.description: LLM-as-a-Judge, Ragas metrics (Faithfulness, Relevance), benchmarks (MMLU, HumanEval), unit testing, and red teaming.
study_notes: Evaluating RAG systems with Faithfulness, Context Recall, and Answer Relevance.
Reducing bias and variance in LLM-as-a-Judge setups.
Automated prompt regressions and CI/CD evaluation test suites.

ai-safety-and-governance.description: Data privacy, PII masking, guardrails (NeMo, Llama Guard), alignment tax, copyright, and responsible AI deployment.
study_notes: Implementing input/output guardrails using Llama Guard or NeMo.
Redacting PII and enforcing data isolation in multi-tenant RAG systems.
Managing the alignment tax: balancing safety interventions with model capability.

interview-experience.description: Role-specific interview blueprints (AI Engineer, FDE, AI Architect), portfolio project presentation, and scenario checklists.
study_notes: Understanding role expectations: AI Engineer vs MLOps vs FDE vs AI Architect.
Structuring project deep-dive presentations to showcase production impact.
Handling scenario-based AI architecture interviews under constraints.
